samples.summary: The verdict string at mark-ready.mjs:183 is now a load-bearing cross-file contract (the promote job `grep -qF`s it to distinguish a gate refusal from a node crash), but the print site carries no note saying so. Editing or reflowing that `console.log` — the kind of edit nobody would think twice about — makes every legitimately-unready PR red the promote job with "mark-ready CRASHED". Every other cross-file contract in this codebase is a named export for exactly this reason (HANDOFF_MARKER in disclosure.mjs, DEFAULT_REVIEW_CHECKS in checks.mjs); this one is a bare literal duplicated into the workflow. The new test does catch drift, so the impact is a confusing CI failure rather than a silent break.

samples.summary: The downstream consumer of the promotion decision — the `Update loop status (promotion)` step — still reports only two possible reasons ("a gate was unsatisfied or the flip failed") in the sticky loop-status comment. This diff adds two new outcomes the promote job can now reach: mark-ready crashed (exit 1 with no verdict line → job exits 2) and an unenumerated status such as 127/128+signal (→ job exits 2). Both fire this step via `if: always()` with `READY` unset, so the human-visible note names causes that are not what happened, which is precisely the mis-attribution the workflow comment at :1511-1517 says it exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The stalled/paging safety-net comment enumerates the ways `promote` can fail and now describes only the pre-change set ("mark-ready exit 2 — e.g. an empty required-check set or another tooling error"). After this change the job also fails on a crashed mark-ready (exit 1 with no verdict line, remapped to 2) and on any unenumerated status (`*)` → 2). The paging behaviour itself is unchanged and correct — only the documentation of what triggers it is out of step.

samples.summary: scripts/agent/mark-ready.test.mjs now pins the promote step's *shell shape* (the exact redirect target, "no `|` anywhere between the invocation and `code=$?`", the `case` label set, and per-branch `exit` counts) in a file that is not the workflow. That makes ordinary edits to `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml`'s promote step fail a node:test in scripts/agent with no local signal — e.g. adding a clarifying comment containing a pipe character (the block already discusses `cmd | tee`) between the invocation and `code=$?` trips `assert.ok(!invocation.includes("|"))` even though the capture is still a redirect. The workflow is the site that will need to change to satisfy an assertion living elsewhere.
